messages:
acme-oncall: dyson-service in our eu-west Private deployment is getting intermittent 502/504 to Redwood control plane since ~08:12 UTC. IKE shows as UP but API requests time out.
miriam: thanks, assigning net oncall. @raj are you free to triage? :eyes: 
raj: taking it. can you paste the DC/VPN identifiers and any recent config changes?
acme-oncall: dx-id dx-euw-ACME-12, vpn gw id vg-45. No config changes on our side since midnight. Logs show "upstream connect error or disconnect/reset before headers" and connection resets every ~30-90s.
raj: first step: check BGP adj and PfxRcd from our edge for that peer and verify IPsec SAs.
raj: running quick checks...
raj: ```
# show ip bgp summary | include ACME
Neighbor        V    AS MsgRcvd MsgSent  TblVer  State/PfxRcd
10.204.8.2      4 64512  12452   12451       0        0
```
raj: neighbor is ESTABLISHED but PfxRcd=0. IKE SAs up, ESP traffic observed on tunnel.
jess: that will explain asymmetric/blackhole behaviour for customer prefixes. If we don't have their routes, return path fails and TCP resets.
miriam: any idea why PfxRcd is zero?
raj: asked ACME to show advertised prefixes. acme-oncall: they are advertising many /32 host routes from their monitoring fabric (10.11.97.0/24 containing many /32s) and show >1100 prefixes on their side.
raj: aha. infra pushed a route-filter tightening earlier at 07:58 UTC that denies prefixes longer than /24 for DX peers. That would drop the /32 adverts.
alex: confirm: I deployed a micro change to inbound prefix-lists to reduce noisy advertisements from a partner. We added `deny prefix length >24` to inbound for several DX neighbors at 07:58.
raj: timeline matches. so our edge sees IKE up, but BGP learns zero prefixes -> traffic to those /32s is unroutable -> intermittent failures when traffic hits services only reachable via those host routes.
acme-oncall: weird that it's intermittent. sometimes calls succeed for minutes.
raj: likely because some destinations either have aggregated /24 adverts or fall back to internet egress paths. Also health-checks and caches cause bursts of successful traffic.
miriam: mitigation?
raj: propose temporary rollback: add an explicit permit for ACME's neighbor or AS to accept longer prefixes, then work with ACME to aggregate to /24s. That avoids a global widen.
jess: agree. add a per-peer exception for dx-euw-ACME-12 and raise infra ticket to improve playbook.
alex: deploying targeted exception now. will patch edge-a then edge-b in eu-west-1. change id cfg-2026-05-12-378.
oncall-bot: deploy started by alex at 08:33:12 UTC
alex: edge-a patched. pinging some of the /32 hosts...
raj: re-checking BGP...
raj: ```
# show ip bgp neighbors 10.204.8.2
    Neighbor is 10.204.8.2, remote AS 64512, established
    PfxRcd: 1124
```
raj: we now see ~1124 prefixes including /32s from ACME.
acme-oncall: testing app now. initially saw a flurry of 504s during the change but traffic steadied. reporting 99.9% success over last 5m.
miriam: great. can we leave the exception in place short-term and ask ACME to aggregate?
jess: long-term fixes: 1) exclude known Private DX peers from blanket prefix-length denies 2) alerting when PfxRcd==0 for >1min 3) docs for customers recommending aggregates (min /24) 4) roll change through infra playbook.
alex: I'll open an infra ticket to add per-peer exceptions, add the alert, and update the maintenance checklist.
raj: recommend we publish guidance: avoid /32s over DX/VPN unless coordinated; use aggregates or explicit route-leak plans.
miriam: ACME, what's your plan?
acme-oncall: we have a maintenance window at 22:00 UTC to consolidate, but can push an aggregation at 14:00 UTC today if that helps. We'll confirm by 12:00.
miriam: please confirm by 12:00 UTC. We'll keep the exception until you verify aggregation. We'll follow up with a short customer note.
acme-oncall: confirmed, will target 14:00 UTC and update here. Thanks for the quick work. App back to normal.
miriam: filing incident follow-ups and comms. Closing the urgent page. :white_check_mark:
